name: Connector practice
brief: Support the flexible cable with one gripper. Use the other to align and seat the USB-C plug in the fixed socket.
hint: Pinch the rear of the black housing, not the metal nose. Approach the socket straight along its axis. Reduce Motion × for fine alignment.

goals.label: Release the plug fully seated in the socket

plan: Use the right gripper to pinch the rear half of the black plug housing on its narrow cradle. Leave the metal nose clear of the fingers.
Lift the plug. With the other gripper, pinch the cable midway to take up its weight and leave a relaxed loop.
Align the flat metal nose with the socket mouth. Keep the plug level and approach straight along the opening.
Advance slowly until the detent seats. Open the plug gripper, then release the cable and let the connector settle.
tips: The socket is hollow, with a centre tongue and solid walls. Lateral or angular error blocks insertion; pulling harder is not alignment.
Turn the wrist 180 degrees to reverse USB-C. A quarter turn cannot fit. Drag empty space to orbit and scroll to zoom.
The cable bends, drags on the table and pulls back on the plug. Lift a slack loop with the second gripper if tension pulls the nose off axis.
TacHammer cues distinguish contact impacts, cable load and the seating click. Enable them in Task settings and map each controller to its wrist or hand.
Hold Shift with W/A/S/D/Q/E for 0.2 mm steps, or with J/K/U/O for fine wrist angles. Motion × 0.1 reduces AprilTag translation for this precision task.
